messages:
janelle-cust: Hey team — hitting a weird combo of issues from our app on Vercel Edge using @redwood/sdk v2.1.0. Streaming responses (ReadableStream) abort ~2–3s in, SDK reports a retry, and we were billed twice for the same user prompt. Minimal repro below, can share logs.

maria-support: Sorry you're seeing that — thanks for reporting. A couple quick things: can you paste the SDK exact version, the Vercel region, and any trace id you see in logs? Also, do you have a proxy or middleware (gzip, compression) in front of the Edge function?

janelle-cust: SDK is @redwood/sdk@2.1.0, Vercel region iad1. Trace header we captured: X-Redwood-Trace: trace-0a1b2c3d. No custom proxy, but we do have a simple middy-style middleware adding CORS and a small body-compression middleware. Repro code (serverless edge):

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
export default async function handler(req) {
  const client = Redwood.createEdgeClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'gpt-open-1', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'echo many times' }] });
  return new Response(stream.body, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' } });
}
```

Logs snippet:
```
fetch upstream iad1 499 mid-stream
redwood-sdk: retrying request id=abc123 attempt=2
readable: stream closed unexpectedly, err=AbortError
```

maria-support: OK that's helpful. Two hypotheses: 1) the edge runtime+compression middleware is closing the pipe when a retry happens, and 2) the SDK auto-retry logic is causing duplicate billing when the upstream response is partial. Can you try setting env var REDWOOD_SDK_DISABLE_AUTO_RETRY=true and repro? That will test the billing side quickly.

janelle-cust: I tried DISABLE_AUTO_RETRY and that stopped the duplicate charge — good. Streaming still aborts mid-chunk though (same AbortError). Interesting bit: downgrading to @redwood/sdk@2.0.4 makes the stream stay open, but we lose the SSE keepalive behavior we rely on. So 2.0.4 = stable stream but less keepalive; 2.1.0 = keepalive + aborts + retries.

ben-runtime: pinging eng-runtime. @sam-eng any idea? Could be the new keepalive/heartbeat code interacting with ReadableLock in edge fetch polyfill.

sam-eng: I can take this. Quick questions: can you run with REDWOOD_LOG=debug and paste the start/finish of the request trace (no PII) and the exact Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding we see? Also, does the compression middleware buffer chunks (i.e., gzip) or just set headers? If it buffers, that could trigger early stream closure.

janelle-cust: Compression is a small middleware that gzips on the fly — doesn't buffer entirely but uses a TransformStream. Pasted debug trace around the failure:

```
[debug] outgoing request id=abc123 -> /v1/chat/stream
[debug] sent first chunk 0 -> upstream 200 OK
[debug] upstream sent event data chunk-1
[debug] upstream sent event data chunk-2
[warn] upstream connection reset by peer (code=ECONNRESET)
[error] readable stream aborted in userland: AbortError
[info] sdk autofallback triggered, creating new request id=abc123-retry
```

sam-eng: That aligns with a case where the upstream connection closes and our retry path spawns a new fetch while the original ReadableStream remains locked/aborted by the runtime's pipe. In Node edge runtimes we sometimes see AbortError when multiple fetches try to pipe into the same response. We're investigating a fix to ensure retries don't race the original stream.

maria-support: I've created internal issue INFR-3289 with the traces and repro steps, tagging runtime and sdk teams. For remediation we recommend: set REDWOOD_SDK_DISABLE_AUTO_RETRY=true (prevents duplicate billing), remove the gzip TransformStream as a test to see if it is the buffer/lock trigger, and if possible try our canary @redwood/sdk@2.1.1-canary.3 which includes a retry locking fix we've been testing.

deploy-bot: deploy(vercel) succeeded — project=customer-xyz env=prod region=iad1 id=deploy_2026_03_17_12_34

janelle-cust: Installing the canary now and will remove the gzip middleware to confirm. If canary fixes streaming + we keep retries disabled, that looks like an acceptable workaround while you patch mainline.

ben-runtime: Also, if you can capture a small HAR (first ~10 KB) of the client->edge->redwood calls, that helps us confirm header/encoding sequence. If you can't attach, paste the request/response headers.

janelle-cust: Will do — headers below (sanitized):
```
:method: GET
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.ai
accept: text/event-stream
connection: keep-alive
accept-encoding: gzip
user-agent: Redwood-Edge/2.1.0
X-Redwood-Trace: trace-0a1b2c3d
```

sam-eng: Perfect — that's actionable. I already have a branch that gates retries behind a lock and ensures original response body is preserved if consumed. We'll try to push a 2.1.1 stable patch after QA. For now: (1) REDWOOD_SDK_DISABLE_AUTO_RETRY=true, (2) try canary 2.1.1-canary.3, (3) if possible temporarily remove gzip TransformStream.

maria-support: Thanks @janelle-cust for quick repro. We'll update INFR-3289 once eng lands a fix. Please ping this thread after testing the canary. :thumbsup:

janelle-cust: Thanks all — applying canary + disabling auto retry now, will report back in ~30m.
